name: Concision and focus
definition: Keep the submission succinct, tightly focused on the rule, and easy for staff to excerpt and address.

name: r4:P11:Traceable Evidence Use
definition: Score whether the comment's factual claims rest on support a reader could locate and check. A 10 identifies specific studies, datasets, statutes, official analyses, or clearly described observations, and explains their relevance and limitations. A 5 points to real sources but leaves their bearing or limits unstated. A 0 leaves claims unsupported or rests them on vague references such as 'studies show'.

name: r1:P09:Substance survives deletion of the position statement
definition: Delete every sentence that states support, opposition, gratitude, feeling, or a purely procedural request, then score what remains. A 10 leaves a body of reasons, facts, or requested changes that stands on its own as regulatory input. A 5 leaves a thin residue: one reason, or a general consideration. A 0 leaves nothing, because the comment consisted entirely of a position, an attitude, an endorsement of someone else's filing, or a scheduling request.

name: r1:P16:Temporal and cumulative effects
definition: Score whether the comment's reasoning extends past immediate impacts to effects over time. A 10 analyzes delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects and says what unfolds over that horizon. A 0 confines its reasoning to a short-term assertion about immediate impact. Score the time horizon actually reasoned about in the text, not whether the analysis is correct.

name: r4:P04:Reasoning-based persuasion vs rhetorical amplification
definition: Score whether the comment's persuasive force comes from developed reasoning and evidence rather than from rhetorical amplification. A 10 rests entirely on developed reasoning or evidence delivered in a measured tone, even when the position is strongly held. A 5 mixes real argument with heated rhetoric. A 0 substitutes capitalized or repeated demands, insults, or hyperbole for any developed argument.

name: r1:P06:Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups
definition: Score whether the comment distinguishes how the rule's impact differs across identified affected groups. A 10 names at least two distinct affected populations or entities and explains how the effect on them differs. A 0 refers only to a single undifferentiated group such as 'the public' or 'everyone', or does not identify who is affected at all. Score the differentiation actually stated in the text.

name: Comment structure, organization, and summaries
definition: Provide a clear introduction stating identity/relevance; an upfront summary of key points; organized sections with headings/bullets and logical flow; and a brief concluding recap/close.

name: Evidence‑supported, verifiable claims
definition: Make specific, checkable assertions supported with credible evidence and clear citations to sources (preferably independent/scientific where relevant).

name: r3:P06:Quantified supporting evidence
definition: Score whether the comment supports its position with numbers. 10 = it uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates that bear on its position and are stated concretely enough to be checked. 0 = it offers no verifiable quantitative support at all.

name: Actionable alternatives and drafting in public comments
definition: Comments propose specific, feasible in‑scope alternatives or ready‑to‑adopt regulatory text (including mitigations), with clear, concrete asks that staff can implement.

name: Provide concrete, decision‑relevant data and examples
definition: Supply on‑the‑ground data, concrete examples, and operational evidence tied to claims, with enough fields to enable agency analysis.

name: Commenter identity, stake, and qualifications
definition: Clearly identify who the commenter is, whom they represent, why they’re affected, and relevant expertise or lived experience; indicate breadth of support or represented constituencies where applicable.

name: Personalization and substance in mass‑comment campaigns
definition: Avoid duplicative form letters and easily detectable templating; enable and submit unique, substantive, human‑authored comments (AI assistance is acceptable when transparently, genuinely used).

name: Evidentiary support and argumentation quality
definition: Present clear, structured claims backed by credible, peer‑reviewed or empirical evidence; use citations and concrete examples; maintain high signal‑to‑noise; anticipate/rebut counterarguments.

name: r1:P17:Quantified scale of real-world impact
definition: Score whether the comment supplies specific, position-relevant numbers establishing the scale of the problem or benefit the rule addresses. A 10 gives concrete, comment-specific figures -- dollar amounts, percentages, counts, timeframes -- that make the magnitude of the issue legible. A 0 gives no numbers at all, or only a generic or borrowed statistic not tied to the specific matter at hand. Score the specificity and relevance of the figures, not whether they favor any side.

name: r1:P19:Verifiable, attributable evidentiary sourcing
definition: Score the extent to which the comment's factual claims are attached to identifiable, checkable sources. A 10 gives specific citations to named studies, agency data, statutes, or official reports that actually support the claim made. A 0 states factual claims confidently with no source, or sources them to non-authoritative or unrelated material such as unnamed blogs, hearsay, or 'as I understand it'. Score the sourcing, not whether you agree with the claim.

name: r4:P25:Specific, precise proposed regulatory fix
definition: Score how specifically the comment states the change it wants made to the proposal. A 10 supplies exact replacement wording, a specific numeric threshold, or an unambiguous procedural modification. A 5 names the direction of the change but leaves its substance unspecified. A 0 states only a general 'for' or 'against' position and offers no specific alternative.

name: Evidentiary rigor and sourcing in comments
definition: Arguments are grounded in specific, credible evidence with clear sourcing and documentation; methods are appropriate; uncertainty is acknowledged; avoid uncited claims and overreach.

name: Concrete, context‑specific, domain‑aware impact evidence
definition: Provide detailed, real‑world examples and technical specifics; localize who/where is affected; include sector‑specific data and practitioner insights to show concrete harms/benefits and implementation implications.

name: r2:P08:Distributional incidence and equity
definition: Score whether the comment differentiates who bears the costs and benefits. Score 10 when it names particular populations, firms, places, or users that face distinct costs or benefits and explains why exposure or access is unequal among them. Score 0 when effects are described only for an undifferentiated public.

name: r3:P11:Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
definition: Score whether the comment offers a worked alternative to the proposal. 10 = it proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why that option can achieve the same regulatory objective, naming the relevant tradeoffs. 0 = it only registers support for or opposition to the proposal as written.

name: r1:P12:Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
definition: Score how fully any alternative approach the comment proposes is specified in the text itself. A 10 lays out the mechanism -- steps, components, numbers, procedure -- in enough detail that another reader could implement or evaluate it. A 0 names an alternative without describing it, or points to a solution held outside the comment ('I already have one, contact me'). A comment proposing no alternative at all also scores 0.

name: r4:P15:Viable alternative design
definition: Score whether the comment offers a practicable alternative regulatory design that still advances the proposal's stated objective while addressing the defect it identifies. A 10 describes such an alternative in enough detail that how it would work is clear. A 5 names an alternative direction without specifying any design. A 0 offers nothing beyond withdrawing the proposal or enforcing it as written.

name: r2:P23:Feasible alternative design
definition: Score whether the comment offers an implementable alternative to the proposal. Score 10 when it proposes a concrete alternative, exception, threshold, or safeguard and explains how that variant still serves the proposal's stated legitimate objective. Score 0 when it offers only support, opposition, or an unelaborated demand. Score in between when an alternative is named but its fit to the objective is left unexplained.
